project.title: Portfolio Editor
project.summary: A shared authoring workspace where people and agents curate evidence into portfolio pages, compare changes, and review the exact public result.

preview.description: The block palette and page structure sit beside the Portfolio Site renderer in the Editor.

blocks.body:
## Turn evidence into a deliberate public page

Portfolio Editor is the private workspace between a record of completed work and the public portfolio. A person or agent can start from a Work Report or create an update, project, or capability directly, then select evidence, rewrite the story, and arrange the page.

The block palette supports text, images, video, galleries, documents, code, diagrams, terminal recordings, comparisons, charts, and references. A live preview uses the actual Portfolio Site renderer, so authoring decisions are visible in the layout that readers will receive.

## Let people and agents work in the same history

The browser, CLI, and MCP interface edit one revisioned Workspace. Each saved action records a meaningful transaction with conflict checks and durable undo and redo. Agent edits first flush pending browser changes, and overlapping edits are rejected instead of overwriting newer work.

File intake commits the owned asset and its page reference together. Selection, panels, and scroll position remain interface state, keeping the document history focused on content.

## Review exactly what will change

The owner can compare the working page with its last accepted version, inspect changed fields and blocks, and restore individual pieces through guarded edits. Exact review freezes the candidate’s content, media, and connections and asks Portfolio Site to validate and render it against accepted context.

Applying that review accepts the identified page and its connections together. A later edit to the candidate or relevant context requires another review. This keeps unrelated drafts outside a page’s approval.

## Keep evidence, approval, and publication separate

Imported Work Reports remain independent source records. Private notes and provenance stay in the Workspace, while only reviewed public material enters the accepted portfolio. Asset intake sanitizes embedded metadata and records a receipt tied to the retained bytes.

Acceptance queues a durable release for preparation. Constellation realizes the prepared site and handles explicit publication as a separate step, allowing the authoring workspace to focus on curation and review.
